title: Uncovering latent urban mobility patterns via smart-card and survey data fusion
authors: Khoa D. Vo; Seung Woo Ham; Mousumi Roy; Swapnil Mishra; Prateek Bansal
abstract: Multiday, multimodal, time-dependent origin-destination (TD-OD) flows describe when, where, and how urban travel occurs. However, existing approaches are typically single-mode or rely on dense multimodal observations that are rarely available at scale. We show that multimodal TD-OD flows can be recovered by integrating household travel surveys with smart-card transit data. The proposed framework estimates cross-modal flow ratios from survey data and applies them to time-varying transit flows to recover private-vehicle and walking demand at hourly and day-of-week resolution. Validation against independent datasets in Singapore and Seoul shows strong agreement (common part of commuters > 0.70; R-squared > 0.60). The recovered flows support policy-relevant analyses, showing that transit is most competitive for intermediate distances (11–16 km) and transit-only data can underestimate peak epidemic infections by up to 50%. These findings demonstrate the importance of a scalable data fusion for multimodal mobility analysis in sustainable and resilient urban planning. This study develops an approach to recover multimodal hourly urban mobility patterns by fusing small-scale surveys with near-census transit data. The method is validated by reconstructing private-vehicle and walking flows in Singapore and Seoul.
abstractZh: 多日、多方式、时变起讫点（TD-OD）流描述城市出行何时、何地以及以何种方式发生。然而，现有方法通常只考虑单一方式，或依赖难以大规模获取的密集多方式观测。我们表明，将家庭出行调查与公交智能卡数据整合，可以恢复多方式TD-OD流。所提框架从调查数据估计跨方式流量比例，将其应用于时变公交客流，从而以小时和星期几为时间分辨率恢复私人车辆与步行需求。基于新加坡和首尔独立数据集的验证显示高度一致性（通勤者共同部分指标大于0.70；R平方大于0.60）。恢复的流量能够支持政策相关分析，显示公共交通在中等距离（11—16公里）最具竞争力，而仅使用公交数据可能将疫情感染峰值低估多达50%。这些发现说明，可扩展的数据融合对于可持续、韧性城市规划中的多方式移动分析具有重要意义。本研究将小规模调查与近乎全量的公交数据融合，提出恢复逐小时多方式城市移动模式的方法，并通过重建新加坡和首尔的私人车辆及步行流量进行验证。
